name: Character Sheet Creator
description: 참고 캐릭터의 의상 정면·캐릭터 후면·얼굴 정면 시트
prompt:
Professional character reference sheet, three views arranged side by side, each occupying approximately one third of the frame width, 16:9 aspect ratio.

All three views share one single continuous muted dark gray background.
No divider lines, no borders, no gaps, no frames, and no separators between the views.
The background flows seamlessly across the entire image as one unbroken space.


REFERENCE FIDELITY:

Use the attached reference image as the authoritative source for both the character and the visual style.

Accurately preserve the character shown in the reference:
same identity,
same gender,
same facial structure,
same facial proportions,
same eyes,
same hairstyle,
same hair color,
same body proportions,
same outfit,
same accessories,
same materials,
same colors,
and same distinctive design details.

Do not redesign, reinterpret, beautify, age, or otherwise alter the character.


STYLE PRESERVATION:

Automatically identify the visual medium, rendering method, and stylistic language of the attached reference image and preserve them consistently in the output.

The generated image must look as though it belongs to the exact same visual world and was created using the same visual approach as the reference.

Preserve the reference image's:
- degree of realism or stylization
- facial stylization
- anatomical stylization
- skin rendering
- eye rendering
- hair rendering
- material rendering
- texture treatment
- shading method
- lighting behavior
- edge treatment
- linework, if present
- color treatment
- contrast
- level of detail
- depth and dimensionality
- overall rendering finish

If the reference is photographic, preserve its photographic appearance.
If the reference is semi-realistic or 2.5D, preserve that same degree of semi-realism.
If the reference is anime or illustrated, preserve its original illustration style and stylization.
If the reference is 3D or CGI, preserve its original 3D rendering characteristics.
If the reference uses another visual medium, preserve that medium accordingly.

Do not convert the reference into a different visual medium or rendering style.
Do not increase or decrease the degree of realism.
Do not translate a stylized character into a realistic human.
Do not stylize a realistic subject into an illustrated or animated character.

When there is any conflict between generic rendering conventions and the attached reference image, always prioritize the reference image.


LEFT VIEW:

Full-body front view.

The outfit is displayed in invisible ghost-mannequin style, as if worn by the character's invisible body.

Use a natural relaxed standing posture.
Arms are positioned naturally downward at the sides rather than in an A-pose or T-pose.

No head, no face, no hair, and no visible neck.

Above the garment's neckline or collar opening there is simply empty background.

Do not show:
a neck stump,
a cut surface,
a severed edge,
exposed flesh,
or visible skin above the collar.

Any body area that would normally be visible through an open or revealing garment should follow the intended ghost-mannequin presentation rather than introducing a visible person.

Preserve the exact outfit construction, silhouette, layering, materials, decorations, and accessories from the reference.


CENTER VIEW:

Full-body back view of the exact same character.

Use the same natural relaxed standing posture.

Keep the character's head in this view.

Show only the back of the head and the hairstyle from behind.
No face is visible.

Accurately reconstruct the hairstyle, hair accessories, outfit structure, silhouette, and costume details from the rear while remaining consistent with the reference image.

Do not invent unnecessary new design elements.


RIGHT VIEW:

One tight chest-up portrait of the exact same character.

Front-facing, looking straight toward the viewer.

The bottom of the portrait is cropped around mid-chest level.

Only the head, shoulders, and upper chest are visible.

Do not show the waist, stomach, hips, or lower torso.

The portrait remains fully contained inside the right one-third section and does not overlap or expand into the other views.

The face should occupy most of the right section.

This is the only view on the sheet where the face is visible.

Expression:
calm neutral expression,
mouth fully closed,
relaxed lips.

Match the face from the reference as closely as possible rather than creating a new interpretation.


CONSISTENCY:

All three views represent the exact same character.

Maintain consistent:
body proportions,
outfit proportions,
hair length,
hair shape,
accessories,
materials,
colors,
construction details,
and visual style across every view.

The different views should feel like multiple views of one single character, not separate variations or redesigns.


COMPOSITION:

Three clearly readable views arranged horizontally:
left — full-body front outfit view,
center — full-body back character view,
right — tight chest-up front portrait.

Each view occupies approximately one third of the total width.

Keep the scale and spacing visually balanced.

Use one continuous background across the full canvas.

No panel borders or visible separators.


OUTPUT RESTRICTIONS:

Absolutely no text.
No labels.
No captions.
No headings.
No watermarks.
No letters.
No numbers.
No logos.
No UI elements.

Visual content only.
